newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open firm on Dow gains, push higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open firm on Dow gains, push higher.

text.p: French shares added one percent to the CAC index in opening trades on Friday, building on Wall Street's overnight runup of 127 points, traders said.
Traders had expected the market to firm and the question was whether the futures contract would decisively break through the 2,300 level in trading today.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 28.07 points or 1.25 percent at 2,276.77 at 0910 GMT, after opening up 0.99 percent. The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,282 from 2,255 on Thursday's close.
Volume was around 155 million francs in early exchanges. By midmorning, turnover was around a solid 3.9 billion francs.
Eurotunnel weakens 1.43 percent to 6.90 francs, following Thursday's small fire on a platform at the Folkestone terminal, which was quickly put out.

Alcatel Alsthom lags market with narrow gain, while Lagardere shows weak tone. The government is now not expected to decide on how Thomson-CSF will be privatised until after the Christmas and New Year holidays.

In the car sector, Michelin drops 1.9 percent to 268.3 francs, seriously bucking the market trend. French car sales are forecast to fall about 10 percent next year, according to the Cofica car loans company.
Michelin has shown recent volatility amid market talk of a capital increase, which the company has denied.
Renault shows its customary weakness, down one percent at 106 francs, while PSA Peugeot Citroen gains 0.89 percent to 567.

"Colossal volume" in Roussel Uclaf, up 5.7 percent at 1,521 francs, as holders selling now will get the cash at the next monthly settlement instead of waiting for payouts at the end of the buy-outoffer period from parent Hoechst, one broker said.
Moulinex up 1.28 percent at 119, ahead of first half 1996/97 results due this afternoon.
